elements.name: Water
elements.info: is life in liquid form. Combine with CO₂ for fizzy chemistry or with metals to see reactions bubble!

elements.name: Carbon Dioxide
elements.info: is a gas from breathing and burning. Mix with water to create carbonic acid fizz!

elements.name: Ammonia
elements.info: is a smelly but useful gas. Combine with oxygen for nitric fun!

elements.name: Hydrogen Chloride
elements.info: is a sharp gas. Drop it in water to get hydrochloric acid power.

elements.name: Methane
elements.info: is a flammable gas, perfect for energy experiments. Combine with oxygen for a fiery show!

elements.name: Sodium Chloride
elements.info: is plain old table salt! Sprinkle a little science on it.

elements.name: Iron Oxide
elements.info: is rusty goodness. Great for experiments or just showing some color.

elements.name: Sodium Hydroxide
elements.info: is a strong base. Handle with care, it can make some bubbly reactions.

elements.name: Calcium Oxide
elements.info: is quicklime. Add water and watch it transform!

elements.name: Calcium Hydroxide
elements.info: is slaked lime. It’s soft, basic, and perfect for chemistry play.

elements.name: Carbonic Acid
elements.info: is fizzy and fun. It forms when CO₂ meets water for a bubbly surprise.

elements.name: Calcium Carbonate
elements.info: is found in chalk and shells. Solid, yet full of chemistry potential.

elements.name: Nitric Oxide
elements.info: is a reactive gas. Combine with oxygen to get nitrogen dioxide for fun experiments.

elements.name: Nitrogen Dioxide
elements.info: is a reddish gas. Mix with water carefully to make nitric acid!

elements.name: Nitric Acid
elements.info: is a strong acid. Very powerful in reactions, but handle with caution.

elements.name: Hydrochloric Acid
elements.info: is a sour and strong acid. Combine with bases for exciting salt water reactions.

elements.name: Salt Water
elements.info: is a simple but classic mixture. Perfect for neutralizing or salty experiments.

elements.name: Sodium Oxide
elements.info: is a reactive solid. Mix with water to create a strong base reaction.

elements.name: Steel
elements.info: is strong and versatile. Combine iron and carbon to create this metallic marvel.

elements.name: Lithium Hydroxide
elements.info: forms when lithium reacts with water, creating a basic solution.

elements.name: Potassium Oxide
elements.info: is an ionic compound formed by the reaction of potassium and oxygen.

elements.name: Barium Hydroxide
elements.info: is a strong base formed when barium reacts with water.

elements.name: Iron Sulfide
elements.info: forms when iron reacts directly with sulfur under heat.

elements.name: Sodium Nitrate
elements.info: is a neutral salt resulting from nitric acid and sodium hydroxide.

elements.name: Calcium Nitrate
elements.info: is a salt created from nitric acid and calcium hydroxide.

elements.name: Calcium Chloride
elements.info: is a white crystalline compound produced from acid-base neutralization.

elements.name: Sulfurous Acid
elements.info: is a weak acid formed by dissolving sulfur dioxide in water.

elements.name: Sulfur Trioxide
elements.info: is a reactive oxide formed when sulfur dioxide reacts with oxygen.

elements.name: Sulfuric Acid
elements.info: is a strong acid formed when sulfur trioxide combines with water.

elements.name: Hydrogen Sulfide
elements.info: is a toxic gas formed by the combination of hydrogen and sulfur.

elements.name: Brass
elements.info: is an alloy of copper and zinc with high malleability.

elements.name: Bronze
elements.info: is an ancient alloy of copper and tin known for its strength and durability.

elements.name: Stainless Steel
elements.info: is a corrosion-resistant alloy of iron and chromium.

elements.name: Gold(III) Chloride
elements.info: is a compound formed when gold reacts with chlorine gas.

elements.name: Organic Compound
elements.info: represents the first step into organic chemistry from simple elements.

elements.name: Reduced Iron
elements.info: is produced when iron oxide is reduced with carbon in smelting.

elements.name: Electrolyzed Water
elements.info: is the result of decomposing water through electrolysis, yielding hydrogen and oxygen.

elements.name: Copper Nitrate
elements.info: is a blue compound formed from copper reacting with nitric acid.

elements.name: Hydrogen
elements.info: is the universe's lightest and most abundant element. It loves teaming up with oxygen to make water!

elements.name: Oxygen
elements.info: fuels life and fire! Combine it wisely to make water or rust some metals.

elements.name: Carbon
elements.info: is the building block of life. From diamonds to fuels, it can shape-shift into many forms.

elements.name: Nitrogen
elements.info: fills most of the air around us. It's chill alone, but combine it with hydrogen to make ammonia.

elements.name: Chlorine
elements.info: is a strong, zesty element! Mix it carefully for salts and cleaning magic.

elements.name: Sodium
elements.info: is a reactive metal that loves water! Combine with chlorine for tasty salt.

elements.name: Iron
elements.info: is sturdy and strong. Combine with carbon to make steel or with oxygen to rust.

elements.name: Calcium
elements.info: builds bones and bricks alike. Combine it with water or carbon dioxide for interesting results.

elements.name: Helium
elements.info: is a noble gas that does not react easily with other elements.

elements.name: Lithium
elements.info: is a soft, reactive metal that reacts with oxygen to form lithium oxide.

elements.name: Beryllium
elements.info: is a hard metal that reacts slowly with water to form beryllium hydroxide.

elements.name: Boron
elements.info: is a metalloid used in glassmaking and reacts with oxygen to form boron trioxide.

elements.name: Fluorine
elements.info: is the most reactive halogen and forms hydrogen fluoride with hydrogen.

elements.name: Neon
elements.info: is a noble gas that glows red in signs and does not form compounds.

elements.name: Magnesium
elements.info: is a light metal that burns bright and forms magnesium oxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Aluminium
elements.info: is a light metal used widely in industry and reacts with chlorine to form aluminium chloride.

elements.name: Silicon
elements.info: is a semiconductor element that combines with oxygen to form silicon dioxide.

elements.name: Phosphorus
elements.info: is a reactive nonmetal that forms phosphorus pentoxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Sulfur
elements.info: is a yellow nonmetal that burns in air to produce sulfur dioxide.

elements.name: Argon
elements.info: is a noble gas that is inert and used in lighting and welding.

elements.name: Potassium
elements.info: is an alkali metal that reacts violently with water to form potassium hydroxide.

elements.name: Scandium
elements.info: is a transition metal that forms scandium oxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Titanium
elements.info: is a strong metal that forms titanium dioxide, a bright white compound.

elements.name: Vanadium
elements.info: is a hard metal forming vanadium(V) oxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Chromium
elements.info: is a shiny metal forming chromium(III) oxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Manganese
elements.info: is used in steelmaking and forms manganese dioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Cobalt
elements.info: is a magnetic metal that forms cobalt(II) oxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Nickel
elements.info: is a corrosion-resistant metal that forms nickel sulfide with sulfur.

elements.name: Copper
elements.info: is a conductive metal that forms copper sulfide with sulfur.

elements.name: Zinc
elements.info: is used in galvanization and forms zinc oxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Gallium
elements.info: is a soft metal that melts in your hand and forms gallium chloride with chlorine.

elements.name: Germanium
elements.info: is a metalloid that forms germanium dioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Arsenic
elements.info: is a toxic metalloid forming arsenic trioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Selenium
elements.info: is a nonmetal forming selenium dioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Bromine
elements.info: is a dark red halogen forming sodium bromide with sodium.

elements.name: Krypton
elements.info: is a noble gas that rarely forms compounds.

elements.name: Rubidium
elements.info: an alkali metal that reacts violently with water to form rubidium hydroxide.

elements.name: Strontium
elements.info: a soft alkaline earth metal that reacts with oxygen to form strontium oxide.

elements.name: Yttrium
elements.info: a transition metal used in electronics and forms yttrium oxide.

elements.name: Zirconium
elements.info: a corrosion-resistant metal forming zirconium dioxide.

elements.name: Niobium
elements.info: a strong metal forming niobium pentoxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Molybdenum
elements.info: a metal used in alloys forming molybdenum trioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Technetium
elements.info: a radioactive metal forming technetium dioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Ruthenium
elements.info: a rare metal forming ruthenium dioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Rhodium
elements.info: a reflective metal used in catalysts, forms rhodium oxide.

elements.name: Palladium
elements.info: a catalyst metal that can form palladium oxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Silver
elements.info: a precious metal forming silver sulfide when reacting with sulfur.

elements.name: Cadmium
elements.info: a toxic metal forming cadmium oxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Indium
elements.info: a soft metal forming indium trichloride with chlorine.

elements.name: Tin
elements.info: a malleable metal forming tin dioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Antimony
elements.info: a metalloid forming antimony trioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Tellurium
elements.info: a brittle metalloid forming tellurium dioxide with oxygen.

elements.name: Iodine
elements.info: a purple halogen forming hydrogen iodide with hydrogen.

elements.name: Xenon
elements.info: a noble gas that rarely reacts, but can form xenon hexafluoride.

elements.name: Cesium
elements.info: an extremely reactive alkali metal that reacts violently with water to form cesium hydroxide.

elements.name: Barium
elements.info: a soft alkaline earth metal that reacts with oxygen to form barium oxide.

elements.name: Francium
elements.info: is an extremely rare and highly radioactive alkali metal. It reacts violently with water and air.

elements.name: Radium
elements.info: is a radioactive alkaline earth metal once used in luminous paints. It glows faintly in the dark.

elements.name: Rutherfordium
elements.info: is a synthetic transition metal with a very short half-life. It has no stable isotopes.

elements.name: Dubnium
elements.info: is a synthetic and radioactive element, belonging to the transition metals.

elements.name: Seaborgium
elements.info: is an artificial heavy element. Its chemistry resembles tungsten.

elements.name: Bohrium
elements.info: is a synthetic radioactive metal similar in chemistry to rhenium.

elements.name: Hassium
elements.info: is a very heavy synthetic metal. It is expected to behave like osmium.

elements.name: Meitnerium
elements.info: is a synthetic element named after physicist Lise Meitner. Its chemistry resembles iridium.

elements.name: Darmstadtium
elements.info: is a synthetic element that decays within milliseconds. It behaves like platinum.

elements.name: Roentgenium
elements.info: is a synthetic element likely similar to gold and copper in chemistry.

elements.name: Copernicium
elements.info: is a superheavy synthetic element. It may behave like mercury or noble metals.

elements.name: Nihonium
elements.info: is a radioactive synthetic element. It is part of the p-block metals.

elements.name: Flerovium
elements.info: is a heavy synthetic element with possible noble metal-like properties.

elements.name: Moscovium
elements.info: is a synthetic element named after Moscow. It’s expected to behave like bismuth.

elements.name: Livermorium
elements.info: is a synthetic element that may behave like polonium or tellurium.

elements.name: Tennessine
elements.info: is a synthetic halogen. It might have chemical properties between astatine and other halogens.

elements.name: Oganesson
elements.info: is the heaviest known element. It may act like a noble gas, but its properties are still uncertain.

elements.name: Lanthanum
elements.info: is a soft, silvery metal that oxidizes rapidly in air. It is the first element of the lanthanide series.

elements.name: Cerium
elements.info: is used in catalysts and alloys. It oxidizes easily and is the most abundant lanthanide.

elements.name: Praseodymium
elements.info: is used in magnets and aircraft engines. It forms green salts when oxidized.

elements.name: Neodymium
elements.info: is used in powerful permanent magnets and lasers.

elements.name: Promethium
elements.info: is a radioactive element used in luminous paints and atomic batteries.

elements.name: Samarium
elements.info: is used in magnets and nuclear reactors. It has high neutron absorption.

elements.name: Europium
elements.info: is used in red phosphors for televisions and LEDs.

elements.name: Gadolinium
elements.info: is used in MRI contrast agents and nuclear reactors.

elements.name: Terbium
elements.info: is used in green phosphors and solid-state devices.

elements.name: Dysprosium
elements.info: is used in magnets, nuclear reactors, and lasers.

elements.name: Holmium
elements.info: is used in magnets and lasers due to its strong magnetic properties.

elements.name: Erbium
elements.info: is used in fiber-optic communication systems and lasers.

elements.name: Thulium
elements.info: is the rarest stable lanthanide and used in portable X-ray devices.

elements.name: Ytterbium
elements.info: is used in lasers and as an alloying agent in stainless steel.

elements.name: Lutetium
elements.info: is the hardest and densest lanthanide, used in catalysts and PET scan detectors.

elements.name: Actinium
elements.info: is a soft, radioactive metal that glows faintly in the dark. It is the first element of the actinide series.

elements.name: Thorium
elements.info: is a radioactive metal used in nuclear reactors and as a potential fuel source.

elements.name: Protactinium
elements.info: is a dense, highly radioactive metal found in uranium ores.

elements.name: Uranium
elements.info: is a heavy metal used as fuel in nuclear power plants and weapons.

elements.name: Neptunium
elements.info: is a radioactive actinide produced from uranium. It can be used to generate plutonium.

elements.name: Plutonium
elements.info: is a highly radioactive element used in nuclear reactors and weapons.

elements.name: Americium
elements.info: is a synthetic radioactive metal used in smoke detectors.

elements.name: Curium
elements.info: is a synthetic radioactive metal that glows in the dark due to intense radioactivity.

elements.name: Berkelium
elements.info: is a synthetic radioactive metal used for research purposes only.

elements.name: Californium
elements.info: is a synthetic element that emits strong neutron radiation, used in neutron sources.

elements.name: Einsteinium
elements.info: is a synthetic radioactive metal named after Albert Einstein.

elements.name: Fermium
elements.info: is a synthetic element discovered in hydrogen bomb debris.

elements.name: Mendelevium
elements.info: is a synthetic radioactive element named after Dmitri Mendeleev.

elements.name: Nobelium
elements.info: is a synthetic element named after Alfred Nobel, used in scientific research.

elements.name: Lawrencium
elements.info: is a synthetic radioactive element and the last of the actinide series.

elements.name: Hafnium
elements.info: is a corrosion-resistant metal used in nuclear control rods and alloys.

elements.name: Tantalum
elements.info: is a dense metal resistant to corrosion, used in electronics and surgical implants.

elements.name: Tungsten
elements.info: has the highest melting point of any metal, used in filaments and tools.

elements.name: Rhenium
elements.info: is a rare, dense metal used in high-temperature superalloys.

elements.name: Osmium
elements.info: is the densest naturally occurring element, used in durable alloys.

elements.name: Iridium
elements.info: is a hard, corrosion-resistant metal used in spark plugs and crucibles.

elements.name: Platinum
elements.info: is a valuable metal used in jewelry, catalysts, and electronics.

elements.name: Gold
elements.info: is a precious metal valued for its luster and conductivity.

elements.name: Mercury
elements.info: is the only metal liquid at room temperature, used in thermometers and switches.

elements.name: Thallium
elements.info: is a soft, toxic metal used in electronics and optical materials.

elements.name: Lead
elements.info: is a dense metal historically used in pipes and batteries, toxic to humans.

elements.name: Bismuth
elements.info: is a brittle metal used in cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, with low toxicity.

elements.name: Polonium
elements.info: is a rare, highly radioactive metalloid discovered by Marie Curie.

elements.name: Astatine
elements.info: is a rare radioactive halogen, one of the least abundant elements on Earth.

elements.name: Radon
elements.info: is a radioactive noble gas formed from the decay of uranium and thorium.
